title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Implementing the Notice on Effectively Resolving the Issue of Judges and Procurators Leaving Their Posts or Resigning Prematurely
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Implementing the "Notice on Effectively Solving the Problems of Judges and Procurators Leaving Their Posts Early and Resigning Early"

Fa [2010] No. 227

To: The High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region for the Production and Construction Corps:

On May 14, 2010, the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security jointly issued the "Notice on Effectively Solving the Problems of Judges and Procurators Leaving Their Posts Early and Resigning Early" (Fa Fa [2010] No. 14, hereinafter referred to as the "Notice"). This Notice is of significant importance for effectively alleviating the acute problems currently faced by people's courts, such as "more cases than judges" and a "shortage of judges in certain age groups," and for ensuring the normal conduct of trial work. To ensure the implementation of the Notice, the following opinions are hereby put forward:

1. Diligently study and deeply understand the essence of the Notice, effectively strengthen organizational leadership, and comprehensively grasp its implementation. Each high people's court shall promptly forward the Notice to the intermediate and basic people's courts within its jurisdiction and, through various channels and forms, strengthen the study, publicity, and organizational implementation of the Notice. The Party leadership groups and political work departments of people's courts at all levels shall proactively report to local Party committees, maintain close contact and communication with the organizational departments of local Party committees, and, in light of local conditions and the actual situation of the court, propose implementation plans for deployment and implementation in accordance with the requirements of the Notice regarding matters such as the extension of the age limit for judges to leave their posts, specific methods for organizing retired judges to assist with work, relevant policies, and deadlines.

2. People's courts at all levels must, in accordance with the requirements of the Notice, strictly implement the national provisions on the retirement age for civil servants. No judge who has not reached the retirement age or does not meet the conditions for early retirement shall be forced to take early retirement or leave the post while receiving benefits. In compliance with the requirements of the Central Committee of the CPC on "rationally using cadres of all age groups and effectively solving the problem of progressively reducing the age limit for leading cadres at different levels," and in accordance with the Notice, taking into account the actual needs of the trial work of people's courts and the professional characteristics of judges, the age for judges to leave their posts early shall be appropriately extended to maximize the role of judges. For judges who have already left their posts early or resigned early, local people's courts at all levels shall, in accordance with the requirements of the Notice, exercise strict management and enforce strict discipline. For judges who have already left their posts early, they must be required to remain in their positions, perform their job duties normally, and fully play their role. For judges who have left their posts early and, after being persuaded, are unwilling to continue serving as judges, their legal positions shall be removed in accordance with the law.

3. After the issuance of the Notice, local people's courts at all levels shall establish a strict and standardized hierarchical filing system for judges who retire early or resign early. Lower-level courts shall, every six months, submit to the higher-level court the relevant approval information for judges who have taken early retirement or early resignation during that period. Higher-level courts shall, in accordance with the Notice, earnestly fulfill their supervisory and administrative responsibilities.

4. In accordance with the requirements of the Notice, careful planning and meticulous organization shall be carried out for the matters related to retired judges assisting with court work. Courts in each region shall, based on the actual circumstances of their respective jurisdictions, adopt various methods and measures to organize retired judges to assist with work. Depending on each individual's circumstances and wishes, they shall be arranged to participate in work such as receiving visitors for case registration and petitioning, pre-trial mediation, and case quality assessment.

5. Strengthen supervision and inspection to ensure the full and strict implementation of the Notice. The implementation of the Notice cannot be achieved without the understanding and support of the organizational and personnel departments of local Party committees at all levels, the standing committees of people's congresses, and all sectors of society. While comprehensively doing a good job of reporting, coordination, communication, and publicity, people's courts at all levels shall carry out step-by-step supervision and inspection. Lower-level courts shall promptly report to the higher-level people's court any issues arising during the implementation of the Notice. Higher-level people's courts have the responsibility to help lower-level courts resolve conflicts and difficulties, promptly monitor the progress of the work, provide full support, and adopt effective measures such as regular annual inspections to urge implementation. From the date of issuance of the Notice, any practices that do not comply with the requirements of the Notice shall be immediately and resolutely corrected. If not corrected in a timely manner, the responsible leading cadres and personnel shall be held accountable. By the end of this year, each high people's court shall inspect the implementation of the Notice by the courts at all levels within its jurisdiction and report the relevant situation to the Supreme People's Court. Next year, the Supreme People's Court will jointly conduct a centralized inspection of the implementation by courts nationwide together with relevant central departments.

6. The political departments of people's courts at all levels shall pay attention to promptly collecting and sorting out the difficulties and problems encountered during the implementation of the Notice, earnestly study and propose countermeasures and suggestions. For major issues involving policy boundaries, they must not act independently and must promptly report them level by level to the Political Department of the Supreme People's Court.

June 21, 2010
